rich_narrative.summary:
HEART Women & Girls is a U.S.-based nonprofit that provides sexual health education, training, and violence prevention for Muslim communities. <cite id="8">Founded in 2010</cite>, the organization works across health education, advocacy, research, and mutual aid delivery. The organization reported <cite id="3">$2,016,799 in total revenue in FY2024</cite>, achieving a 34.0% 3-year revenue growth trajectory from <cite id="3">$1,123,502 in 2022</cite>.

HEART directs resources into direct survivor support alongside broader education initiatives. In recent program cycles, the group distributed <cite id="5">$350,000 in total direct financial assistance through mutual aid funds</cite>, including <cite id="6">$50,000 redistributed directly to survivors of gender-based violence</cite>. Institutional partnerships also expand its educational reach; HEART trains <cite id="5">750 service providers and community leaders on gender-based violence</cite> and reaches <cite id="5">10,000 incoming students annually through a partnership with the University of Michigan</cite>.

In FY2024, HEART maintained <cite id="3">a 78.3% program expense ratio</cite>, allocating <cite id="3">over three-quarters of its budget directly to program services</cite>. While this ratio beats the 75.0% general nonprofit benchmark, it sits below the peer median of 90.5% for international and global education groups. Financial management is characterized by high liquidity, with <cite id="1">25.6 months of working capital held in working capital</cite>. HEART operates as <cite id="2">a zakat-eligible entity</cite>, accepting zakat for redistribution to designated categories including low-income survivors and individuals in acute financial hardship.
